title: One Practice Card, Ten Words: The Kiosk Drills Faster Now | vitalii.no
description:
Every practice card on our TV wall asked about exactly one compound word, one maths fact, or one vocabulary word, then got shelved until its next turn days later. With eight compound words or eight mental-maths facts queued up for a kid in a single sitting, cycling through one card at a time wasted screen-time minutes repeating the same walk-and-pick flow instead of actually drilling.

I added list-shaped practice cards: compound words and mental-maths facts now hold eight items per card, and vocabulary plus past-tense forms are bundled as wordlist cards holding ten pairs. The kiosk now tracks repetition at the per-word level inside Supabase instead of per card, so a kid sees the word he's actually due for first, not whichever one happened to come up next in rotation. Words that already have their own approved scene stay as single cards, and card sizing scales with how many items are on it.

A single compound-word or mental-maths card now covers eight items, and a vocabulary card covers ten, instead of each item needing its own turn in the walk.
